name: Weathering (corrosion) of antique glass
describes: Water leaches alkali from a glass surface; on unstable glasses this leaves a hydrated, crazed layer, crusts of salts and pits. Medieval potash glass with little silica decays badly; 19th-century soda-lime glass, with more silica, is far more durable, so Victorian windows mostly show soiling rather than crusts, with occasional pitting (flashed ruby is prone). Pits range from about 0.1 mm to 2-4 mm across.

composition.text: Potash glass is 'more prone to deterioration and was later abandoned'; early glass with a low silica ratio 'is more prone to decay than later 19th and early 20th century glass'; soda-lime glass has 13-17 % Na2O.
composition.source: D. Anderson, 'Stained Glass and its Decay', The Building Conservation Directory (1996), https://www.buildingconservation.com/articles/glassdecay/glassdecay.htm
